newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: SEC lifts share suspension of Centennial.
newsitem.headline: SEC lifts share suspension of Centennial.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Friday it had withdrawn its directive to the Philippine Stock Exchange to suspend trading in shares of Centennial City.
The SEC said the order comes after the firm's major shareholders agreed not to divest their stakes in Centennial City without prior approval of the regulator.
Officials at the Philippine Stock Exchange said the bourse would make an announcement about Centenial shares on Monday.
The SEC had ordered the bourse to suspend Centenial shares from trading on Wednesday for possible violation of full-disclosure rules in connection with a 750-hectare reclamation project.
Centennial is part of the Amari consortium which won the right to develop and reclaim land along Manila Bay but the award was questioned by a senator who claimed the government got a low price.
The Amari consortium has denied any wrongdoing.
But the controversy had affected the stock and its price fell to 2.80 pesos on Wednesday from 4.40 pesos on November 29.
Guoco Holdings (Philippines) Inc, one of Centennial's major shareholders, said on Thursday it had no intention to sell its stake in the firm.
Guoco owns 1.5 billion shares of Centennial's outstanding four billion shares.
Centennial holds 20 percent in the Amari consortium while Thai construction firm Italian-Thai Development Plc is the other major stockholder.
